# Tuskers' Code of Conduct

Tusk's Tomes is built for kitchen-table tabletop groups, and the community
around it should feel like one: welcoming, generous with help, and happy
to see new faces — whether you're a 20-year DM or a brand-new player
opening your first terminal.

## Our pledge

We — maintainers, contributors, and community members — pledge to make
participation in the Tusk's Tomes project and any future community
spaces (a Discord server is on the [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md)) a
harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size,
visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic
status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual
identity and orientation.

## What we expect

- **Be kind.** Most people asking for setup help have already tried for
  an hour. Assume good faith.
- **Be patient with newcomers.** Tusk's Tomes is explicitly aimed at DMs
  who've never run `git pull`. If a question sounds basic, answer it
  graciously — that's the audience.
- **Be specific.** "It doesn't work" is hard to help with; logs, OS,
  Node/Python versions, and the exact step that broke are gold.
- **Disagree well.** Critique ideas, not people. PR reviews and roadmap
  debates should leave the other person wanting to come back.
- **Give credit.** If someone's chronicle, glossary, or PR taught you
  something, say so.

## What is not OK

- Harassment, insults, slurs, or personal attacks of any kind
- Sexualised language or imagery, or unwelcome sexual attention
- Doxxing, sharing other people's private information, or posting their
  campaign material without consent
- Sustained disruption of issues, PRs, or any future community threads
- Advocating for or encouraging any of the above

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies in all project spaces — the GitHub repo
(issues, PRs, discussions, code comments), the [feedback form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxdqOhb1SQvI3fs50gMJv_Cesh2MuxUm95QO2iZia5sFhyyQ/viewform?usp=header),
and any other channel that represents the project (including the
community Discord once it launches — see the [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md)).
It also applies when an individual is officially representing the
project in public spaces.

## Enforcement

Report violations through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting
(repository → **Security** tab → **Report a vulnerability**) — it works
for conduct reports too and keeps the report private with the
maintainers. Alternatively, use the [feedback form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxdqOhb1SQvI3fs50gMJv_Cesh2MuxUm95QO2iZia5sFhyyQ/viewform?usp=header)
for non-sensitive concerns. Once the community Discord launches, a
DM-to-a-moderator route will be added; this section will be updated to
include it. All reports will be reviewed and investigated promptly and
fairly.

Maintainers may take any action they deem appropriate, up to and
including a permanent ban from the project and community spaces.
